summary: The Carbonária was a secret society organised in cells on the Italian model. In the last years of the monarchy it became the armed arm of Portuguese republicanism. Its members supplied and sheltered the gunmen who killed Carlos I and his heir in 1908. They also provided much of the street force of the revolution of October 1910. The literature dates its founding and its dissolution only loosely, so the interval here is a range at each end. It is in the atlas because the republican movement acted through it before it acted through a parliament.
